newsitem.title: USA: NYC and lower suburbs carry New York's green bond.
newsitem.headline: NYC and lower suburbs carry New York's green bond.

text.p: New York State's $1.75 billion green bond, which will raise funds to clean air, water and land, won due to the strong backing it got in New York City and the lower suburbs, a state official said on Wednesday.
"It was mostly upstate that said no," said a spokesman for the Board of Elections, Lee Daghlin.

Supporters of the environmental bond issue have sharply criticized one of the opposing groups, CHANGE-NY, for running what they said where misleading advertisements that said New York City would get more than $1.3 billion of the bond's funds.

CHANGE-NY, the state's largest association of taxpayers, has defended its ads. It said they were based on material provided by the Pataki Administration and one of the groups pushing for the act, though it had withdrawn the release used by CHANGE-NY.
With around 15,151 precints of New York's total of 15,487 precints reporting, the state-wide talley stood at 2,039,904 in favor and 1,582,125 against.
The official noted that in Westchester, just north of New York City, the breakdown was around 133,000 in favor and 66,000 against.
A similar pattern was seen in some key counties on Long Island, he added, with Suffolk approved the measure by around two-to-one, and Nassau supporting it by a bigger winning margin.
In New York City's five boroughs, around 806,084 of the voters said yes, with 241,599 against.

The spokesman added that the final numbers likely will be adjusted slightly as the rest of the votes are counted. No results have been received from Ontario County, but it only has 85 election districts, he said, adding he had no explanation immediately available for why it was running so late.
